studies.label: Crosslinking builds ECM network connectivity (real TST-MD, 2D)

nodes.label: The real TST-MD engine reproduces the DIRECTION of the 3D paper's remodeling ...
nodes.statement: The real TST-MD engine reproduces the DIRECTION of the 3D paper's remodeling result in 2D: a contractile cell contracts against the crosslinked ECM (13135 -> ~10 lattice sites) and reorients fibers toward itself (q/q0 1.00 -> ~1.09).

nodes.label: At this parameter regime the cell's equilibrium area is set by its target are...
nodes.statement: At this parameter regime the cell's equilibrium area is set by its target area (10), not by ECM resistance — so this study demonstrates the contraction + reorientation MECHANISM, not the quantitative ECM-limited-equilibrium relationship of Fig 2. Closing that gap requires model calibration (physical->ymmsl unit scaling); documented as the investigation's open calibration item.

nodes.label: Crosslinking sharply raises ECM network connectivity: the giant component jum...
nodes.statement: Crosslinking sharply raises ECM network connectivity: the giant component jumps from 0.0007 (no crosslinks) to 0.18 at ~400 crosslinks and ~0.29 at >=1600 — the percolation-onset mechanism behind Fig 2B.

nodes.label: Connectivity saturates near 0.29 at these reduced fiber/crosslink densities r...
nodes.statement: Connectivity saturates near 0.29 at these reduced fiber/crosslink densities rather than reaching full percolation (~1.0 at the paper's HPC scale). The ONSET direction is reproduced; the full percolated regime needs near-paper-scale networks (a documented scope/calibration limit).
